defects.title: Drawings whose annotation is stroke-font polylines (NIST D2MI, Siemens NX) are classed as vector text: no OCR runs, nothing is read, and no warning says so
defects.scenario: Read the six NIST D2MI drawings (827-9999-903..908), alone (read-one.mts) and attached to their STEP on /api/cad/analyze
defects.expected: Sheets classed text-as-curves (or mixed) and OCR'd; failing that, a warning that the annotation was not read
defects.actual: Every sheet 'vector-text' (3 text runs: the NX plot stamp 'Scale= 0.5000:1', '20150310.1524 [NX8] File: …', 'tamatusk'); 0 parameters; warnings []; ocrWouldRead false so the server never queues OCR. 350 truth items (title block, 6061-T6/T651 material, ASTM standard, chromate conversion coating, dimensions, GD&T) - 0 found. The engineer sees a drawing with no readings and no reason.
evidence: runs/scripts/sheet-stats.mts output: {pathOps:2968, glyphLikePaths:0, imageCoverage:0, textChars:67, textItems:3} -> classify 'vector-text'
defects.rootCause: server/drawing/ingest.ts:88 — textChars >= 25 (the plot stamp alone) returns 'vector-text' unless glyphLikePaths >= 20; stroke-font text is short line segments, not glyph-sized closed outlines, so glyphLikePaths = 0 although pathOps = 2,968. isMixedSheet (ingest.ts:104-106) needs glyphLikePaths >= 20 too, so no 'partly curves' warning and ocrWouldRead (index.ts:46-50) is false.
defects.evidenceFinal: Stroke-font sheets are now classed text-as-curves, OCR'd, and warned about ("only 67 characters of selectable text … beside 2968 pieces of line work"). D2MI recall 0 % → 10 %, but precision 20 % (35 correct, 139 wrong, all needs-validation OCR, mostly dimensions with one-digit nominals); the 6061-T651 title block of 904 is still not read. OCR time on D2MI went from ~1.4 s to 10–27 s per file.

defects.title: Scanned sheets carrying a scanner OCR text layer are read as EXACT text when the page has more than 20 path operators
defects.scenario: NTRS Stirling report pages 159, 161, 163, 170 (full-page image + invisible scanner OCR layer + 28-120 path ops); also on the original 359-page report pages
defects.expected: Classed 'scanned', the scanner layer ignored (index.ts:114 already does this when detected) and the page OCR'd by the reader with 'needs validation' readings
defects.actual: Classed 'vector-text'; scanner OCR garbage becomes method 'pdf-text', reliability 1, status 'extracted' (shown as exact text): thread 'M1' from 'M1 I.JlL-6a', dimensions 80020 from '80020~', 611 from '0611_..-', nominal 0 from '0 -' and '00'. Pages 172 / 200 (pathOps 0 / 11) are handled correctly. None of these readings answers a costing question, so no £ moved, but the provenance shown to the engineer is false.
evidence: sheet-stats.mts: p159 {pathOps:28, imageCoverage:1, textChars:189} -> 'vector-text', scannerLayer false; p172 {pathOps:0} -> 'scanned'
defects.rootCause: server/drawing/ingest.ts:96-98 hasScannerTextLayer requires pathOps < 20; ingest.ts:87 sends a full-page image with >= 60 text chars to 'scanned' only through that test.
defects.evidenceFinal: Stirling p159/161/163/170 now classed scanned, the scanner layer ignored with a warning and the page re-OCR'd; no reading is presented as exact text. Stirling recall 1.1 % → 2.1 % (SIS 2541 read on p159/p161).

defects.title: Material designation read on 0 of 24 genuine drawings that state one (recall 0/37 material facts); the drawing never answers the material question on any genuine pair
defects.scenario: Extraction scoring (44 truth files) and the 9 costing pairs
defects.expected: Common real-world forms read: 'Material: 5052 H-32 Aluminum', '304 Stainless Steel', '303 SST', '(.1195 THICK) 11 GA 304 SST SHT, ASTM A240', 'Mat: 1.2510', 'Mat: Brass', 'Mat: Steel', '6061' in a GB title block
defects.actual: None read as material.designation. Probe (runs/scripts/probe-material.mts): '5052 H-32 Aluminum' -> [], '304 Stainless Steel' -> [], '303 SST' -> [], '6061' -> [], '6061铝' -> [], 'Brass' -> [], 'Steel' -> [], 'SIS 2541' -> []; '1.2510' only with weak hits allowed, but 'Mat:' is not a recognised label so weak hits are never allowed there. The text WAS read (exact text on SeedMint / OpenEAI; OCR on LulzBot, e.g. '2 Material: 5052 H-32 Aluminum' at 97 %). Consequence: every genuine pair keeps the CAD-only material assumption (POM-C acetal on three aluminium parts, steel DC04 on the 5052 sheet parts); answering the family by hand from the drawing moves the cost +29.7 % to +57.5 % (costing.json Chand).
defects.rootCause: server/drawing/extract/material.ts:144 MATERIAL_LABEL accepts MATERIAL / MAT'L / WERKSTOFF / HALBZEUG but not 'MAT:'; MATERIAL_GRAMMARS (from :22) require AA alloys with a temper written '-H32' / '-T6' (not 'H-32' or bare '6061'), AISI/SAE prefixes for 300-series stainless, and have no trade-name entries (brass, steel, aluminium).
defects.statusFinal: FIXED on this set (not independently held out)
defects.evidenceFinal: Material group 0/37 → 32/37 correct, 0 wrong (recall 86.5 %, precision 100 %). Still missed: D2MI 904 6061-T651 / ASTM B205 (stroke font), Stirling p163 NIMONIC 80A, OpenEAI 02-03 7075 (only 6061 read). The fix was developed against these same 44 drawings, so this is a development-set figure.

defects.title: Correcting a misread material designation does not re-interpret the material family the reader derived from it: a stale 'steel' stays on the panel as a leaning for the material question
defects.module: server/drawing/extract/material.ts (material.family emitted with no derivedFrom) + src/engine/engineering-data/overrides.ts (correct)
defects.scenario: LulzBot electronics chassis sheet 1: OCR reads '5052' as '30W9'; the reviewer corrects the designation to 5052 (drawingReview correct op); /reanalyze
defects.expected: The family interpreted from '30W9' (steel) is withdrawn and re-interpreted from '5052' (aluminium), as the design states ('correcting a reading re-runs its interpretation')
defects.actual: drawing:material.designation:1 = '5052' status corrected; drawing:material.family:1 = 'steel' (rawText '30W9', 'From the form of the designation "30W9"') still needs-validation and still offered as the leaning for material.family; the corrected '5052' produces no family and answers no question (a careful reviewer has to reject the stale family and answer the family by hand).
evidence: runs/scripts/manual-review.json (the reject the reviewer had to add)
defects.rootCause: server/drawing/extract/material.ts:180-183 pushes material.family (kind 'interpreted') with no derivedFrom link to the designation; src/engine/engineering-data/overrides.ts:105-117 re-interprets only parameters whose derivedFrom chain reaches the corrected id, so the reader's own family is neither replaced nor reopened (material.condition at :184 has the same shape).
defects.evidenceFinal: Correcting the chassis designation "5052 H32 AL" to "S235JR" re-interprets the family aluminium → steel; no stale family stays live (reconciliation-final correction-supersedes-family PASS).

defects.title: Reports do not say who confirmed or corrected a reading, or when; the correction reason is not printed
defects.module: src/export/drawing-spec-report.ts (DrawingSpecRow) -> core PDF §3, audit pack §9c, workbook 10-Drawing
defects.scenario: Bed plate C costing exported from the screen (runs/exports-c/): 2 corrections, 7 confirmations, 1 conflict settled
defects.expected: The drawing specification table shows each decision's status AND who / when (the history the server stamps: by = signed-in user, at = server clock), and the correction's reason
defects.actual: Rows carry group, parameter, value, source, status ('Corrected' / 'Confirmed'), used — no who, no when, no reason, in all three exports. Only the settled conflict prints 'Settled by qa@test' (no date). The server does hold by/at (engineeringData.parameters[].history).
defects.rootCause: src/export/drawing-spec-report.ts:14-24 — DrawingSpecRow has no by / at / reason fields; buildDrawingSpecReport (:60-77) never reads parameter.history.
defects.evidenceFinal: Core PDF, audit pack and 10-Drawing print "Corrected by qa@test on 10 Nov 2026 11:37 UTC (was "lofl") — as written on the drawing (truth file)" and "Confirmed by … on …"; a settled conflict prints who and when (exports-final/check.json).

defects.title: Model revision is never compared with the drawing revision
defects.scenario: SeedMint assembly STEP (PRODUCT 'Base v12', 'Slider v9') with Base Drawing (V10) and Slider Drawing A3 (V22); D2MI 904 (file 'rev c', title block A); LulzBot washer (STEP rev_IR = drawing IR)
defects.expected: The model's revision (STEP product version / file-name revision) set against the title-block revision; a mismatch raised as a conflict or warning
defects.actual: No CAD-side revision parameter on any case; only the drawing's own revision is listed (V10, V22). Nothing flags the mismatch.
defects.rootCause: from-cad.ts emits identity from the STEP product name only (title.partName); no revision is taken from the STEP PRODUCT version string or file name, so reconcile.ts has nothing to compare.
defects.evidenceFinal: Unchanged: no model revision is extracted; SeedMint Base v12 v V10 and Slider v9 v V22 pass silently.

defects.title: A drawing paired with the wrong model is not detected unless hole callouts were read; overall size / thickness are never compared
defects.scenario: (a) nist-ftc-09 drawing on the ftc-10 model; OpenEAI JXS-01-02 drawing on the JXS-05-01 model; also bed-plate drawing on D2MI 906, ftc-10 drawing on CTC-01
defects.expected: Identity, envelope / stock-thickness and feature mismatches flagged
defects.actual: ftc-09 -> ftc-10 and JXS-01-02 -> JXS-05-01: 0 conflicts, 0 callouts without a model feature (FAIL). bed-plate -> D2MI 906: 2 callouts not in the model + a thread-count conflict (PASS, but the part-name conflict also appears with the RIGHT model because the LulzBot STEPs declare 'ASSEMBLY', so it is not a pairing signal). ftc-10 -> CTC-01: 11 callouts 'no hole of Ø… in the 3D model', no identity conflict (PARTIAL). part.envelope from the kernel is never compared with anything; the drawing's stated stock thickness is not read (D03) so the bend-pair gauge is never cross-checked.
defects.rootCause: reconcile.ts compares only hole / thread callouts against the feature table (:174-297) and whole-part names; no drawing overall-size reading exists to set against part.envelope (from-cad.ts:49).
defects.evidenceFinal: A wrong model now raises a stock-thickness conflict when the drawing states a thickness (FTC-09 drawing on the FTC-10 model: 4.5 mm v 3.0353 mm). Still nothing on the OpenEAI 01-02 drawing / 05-01 model; no identity or envelope comparison; no pairing warning.

defects.title: (CAD-only, pre-existing) A part-number prefix 'PP-' is read as polypropylene and the material family is pre-answered 'plastic' and shown as ANSWERED
defects.scenario: LulzBot bed_plate_v4.5_PP-MP0108.step and corner_bracket_v2.0_PP-MP0106.step, CAD only
defects.expected: No material assumed from a part number; the family question asked (or a name leaning shown, not an answer)
defects.actual: material.family = plastic with source 'answered' in the comparison spec; costed in POM-C acetal stock without any question; the aluminium plate costs £17.30 (bed plate) / £3.50 (bracket). The engineer answered nothing.
evidence: runs/costing.json parts lulzbot-taz6-bed-plate / corner-bracket A.spec = [{material.family: Plastic, answered}]
defects.rootCause: src/engine/material-family.ts:20 matches \bpp\b in the file name ('PP-MP0108' -> 'pp mp0108'); server/routes/cad.ts:2192-2205 answersFromContext turns the filename family into answers['material.family'].
defects.evidenceFinal: The fix strips "PP-"/"PC-" only at the START of a file name; the LulzBot files bed_plate_v4.5_PP-MP0108.step, corner_bracket_v2.0_PP-MP0106.step and bed_leveling_washer_v2.0_PP-MP0082_rev_IR.step still give familyFromFilename = plastic, pre-answered and shown as "answered" (A unchanged: £17.2984 / £3.4967; regression-final.json). src/engine/material-family.ts:22-23 (/^(pp|pc)[-_]/ anchored at ^).

defects.title: (CAD-only, pre-existing) Blank development runs on the server's event loop for ~40 s: the server stops answering, and a client's next request on a kept-alive socket is reset (ECONNRESET)
defects.scenario: LulzBot electronics chassis (1.5 MB STEP, bent sheet) /api/cad/analyze and /reanalyze with the sheet route
defects.expected: Long geometry work off the event loop; other requests (health, other users) served
defects.actual: /api/health took 35.2 s and failed while the chassis was analysed (runs/logs/event-loop-probe.json); 'blank developed from the solid in 39-45 s' in the server log; three runs of the chassis C costing got ECONNRESET on the next /reanalyze until the client retried (costing.json connectionResetsRetried).
evidence: server.log lines '[cad] blank developed from the solid in 42497 ms'
defects.rootCause: server/services/blank-development.ts:58 developed = developBlank(mesh.mesh) — synchronous Tutte/ARAP unfold + forming inverse (server/utils/blank-unfold.ts:605) in the request handler's thread.
defects.evidenceFinal: server/services/blank-development.ts unchanged since e72adf46; the chassis C run again needed no retry this time but the synchronous developBlank call is the same.

defects.title: (CAD-only, pre-existing) Route leaning contradicts the tool's own plausibility guard on sheet parts
defects.scenario: Electronics chassis (2 mm bent shell): leaning 'machining' -> refused 'thin shell rarely machined from solid'; sheet route on the flat 304 plate ftc-09 (84 % fill) and the electronics cover (99 % fill) -> refused 'near-solid part inconsistent with the thin-wall process'
defects.expected: The leaning is a route the guard accepts; a flat or bent constant-gauge plate is accepted for sheet metal
defects.actual: Chassis cannot be costed on the leaning route; ftc-09 and the cover cannot be costed as sheet metal at all (refused in A and C) — the drawing's stock thickness (2.03 mm, .1195 in) could not help.
evidence: runs/costing.json parts lulzbot-taz6-electronics-chassis (A refused), nist-ftc-09@sheet, lulzbot-taz6-electronics-cover@sheet
defects.rootCause: not traced to a line (out of the drawing feature's scope); the 'near-solid' test uses bounding-box fill, which is high for any flat plate.
defects.evidenceFinal: Chassis machining, cover @sheet and FTC-09 @sheet refused by the route guard in A and C again.

defects.title: Split hole callouts raise false count conflicts: each callout's count is compared with the model's total for that diameter
defects.scenario: nist-ftc-07 (inch drawing, vector) with its STEP
defects.expected: Callouts of the same diameter summed (1 + 2X + 4X + 1 = 8) before comparing with the model's 8 × Ø6.35; no conflict
defects.actual: 4 conflicts the engineer must settle: 'the drawing calls 2 × Ø6.35 and the 3D model has 8 × Ø6.35', '4 × Ø6.35 v 8', '2 × Ø15.0876 v 4 × Ø15.08' (twice). Units are handled correctly (inch converted to mm, exact factor, then matched); the converted value is printed unrounded (Ø15.0876, Ø7.137400000000001 in notes).
defects.rootCause: src/engine/engineering-data/reconcile.ts:218-231 — byCount(atDia, h.count) per callout and flagConflict on countDiffers; no aggregation of callouts sharing a diameter.
defects.statusFinal: FIXED for hole callouts; one residual
defects.evidenceFinal: FTC-07: 4 false conflicts → 0 ("one of 4 callouts of Ø6.35 …"). FTC-10 still raises "2 × Ø6 v model 4 × Ø6": the other two Ø6 ±0.15 on the sheet are read as diameter DIMENSIONS, which the new sum does not count (reconcile.ts sameSize filters name === hole.diameter).

defects.title: Reader attaches flag-note numbers to callouts and truncates a leading digit
defects.expected: '8X Ø2.5 ±0.15' (flag note 4 beside it); general tolerance 'profile 1.5 A B C APPLIES TO ALL UNTOLERANCED SURFACES'
defects.actual: hole.diameter {diameter 2.5, count 8, upper 0.154, lower -0.154} from '8X Ø2.5 ±0.154' (the flag digit became a tolerance digit — a wrong VALUE, status extracted); 'Ø3.5 G6 4'; tolerance.general '.5 A B C APPLIES TO ALL UNTOLERANCED SURFACES' (the '1' lost).
defects.rootCause: not traced to a line; the flag number is a separate text run on the same baseline and is concatenated by line assembly (server/drawing/text-lines.ts).
defects.evidenceFinal: FTC-10: "8X Ø2.5 ±0.15" read with ±0.15 (was ±0.154); the general tolerance keeps "1.5".

defects.title: Shipped accuracy script mislabels a file's content class when the truth's `files` map is keyed by another file name
defects.scenario: Scoring NIST CTC/FTC truths beside a copy named <id>.pdf (truth `files` keyed 'nist_ftc_0x_asme1_rx.pdf')
defects.actual: Falls back to 'vector' (name has no '.curves.'), so the shipped table puts 9 curves files in the vector row (per-file counts are unaffected; runs/scripts/score.mts takes the class from the truth's own value).
evidence: runs/logs/shipped-scorer.json table keys v runs/extraction.json totals.byClass
defects.rootCause: scripts/drawings/accuracy-lib.ts:134-139 looks the class up by the scored file's name only.
defects.evidenceFinal: scripts/drawings/accuracy-lib.ts unchanged (class by scored file name).

defects.title: The machining route costs the material FAMILY only: a stated grade on the drawing (304 stainless, 6061-T6, 5052-H32) is replaced by the representative grade (EN8 / 080M40 carbon steel, 6082-T6 bar)
defects.module: machining rule pack / engineering-data adapter (no grade question on machining)
defects.scenario: FTC-09 (304 SST sheet) and the aluminium parts, machining route, with the material confirmed
defects.expected: The stated grade, or a visible alert that the costed grade differs from the drawing's
defects.actual: FTC-09 C costs "EN8 / 080M40 (Medium Carbon)" for a drawing that says 304 stainless (the panel / report say "the grade it names is not costed — the machining route has no grade question and costs the family's representative grade"). Stated, but the cost carries a different material from the drawing.
defects.rootCause: not traced to a line: the machining pack exposes material.family only

defects.title: "5052 H-32 Aluminum" maps to no sheet grade ("5052 H32 AL" does): the grade question stays at the default AA5754-H22
defects.scenario: LulzBot corner bracket, sheet route, designation confirmed
defects.expected: AA5052-H32 Sheet, as for the chassis
defects.actual: No material.grade interpretation; costed AA5754-H22 (corner bracket @sheet C £0.6510)
defects.rootCause: not traced to a line: the hyphen in the temper ("H-32") is accepted by the reader grammar but not by the grade matcher

defects.title: OCR of stroke-font sheets produces many wrong dimension readings (D2MI: 139 wrong v 35 correct)
defects.expected: OCR readings mostly correct, or not offered
defects.actual: Overall strict precision fell 83.3 % → 69.1 % and curves precision 82.2 % → 57.4 %, almost all from D2MI OCR dimensions (e.g. nominal 7, 6, 4, 2 from single digits). All are needs-validation and none reaches the cost, but each is a row an engineer must reject.
defects.rootCause: stated as a follow-up in commit 2a4b54c2
defects.statusFinal: NEW (side effect of the D01 fix)

defects.title: On the screen the material DESIGNATION reading has no Confirm button (only its interpreted family does)
defects.scenario: Bed plate C review through the panel
defects.expected: The engineer confirms the designation as written
defects.actual: "no confirm button for drawing:material.designation:1"; the row sits under "Material as written" with "the grade it names is not costed". Confirming the derived family gives the same cost as the API review (screen £24.92 = API C £24.9246), so no £ effect; the designation shows "Needs checking" in the reports.
defects.rootCause: not traced; the row is rendered in the not-costed list
